Correlating the two within EgressBlockWindow reclassifies the stop: the stage's own *-failed marker, with the host and the exact proxy.domains line to add as the blocker's release condition, kind unavailable-dependency. It charges NOTHING — an outage never spends the budget a real failure needs, and this is not a failure of the work either — and it is said ONCE, under the same stageAlreadyFailed guard every other *-failed post takes. No relaunch follows, because a policy denial does not come back on its own, and that refusal is PERMANENT rather than time-bound: recoverableFailure (board_reconcile_failed.go) reads egressBlockedGaveUp before it reads the stage's own age window, so the ordinary retry paths never resume on this marker even after the block record itself has aged out or a restart has cleared it from memory — the release is a person editing proxy.domains, restarting the daemon, and then issuing the stage's own Retry gesture, which is the same in-place relaunch every other stopped card takes. Two endings are deliberately NOT reclassified: a model-boundary pause (rate limit, overloaded, 5xx, auth refusal), which classifyUnavailability has already diagnosed from the hook's own errorType, and an ending whose refused host is not a plausible hostname — the SNI is container-controlled bytes and is discarded rather than printed into a marker body. Split into one event per stage, matching the src groups the ordinary implementation-failed/planning-failed/review-failed/deploy-failed events already use, rather than one event spanning every stage against every marker: the wider shape (mirroring substrate-unreachable's) let `Accepts("planning", "implementation-failed")` become true and silently absorbed an unrelated, already-documented corpus violation. Distinct from not_states / `a host that cannot launch`, which is the SAME condition caught BEFORE a stage starts (the egress doctor check, SC-4819): there no stage ran and no ticket is blamed, here a stage ran and reported what it saw.
events.prompt: shared/exit-contract.md and human-deploy-fixer-agent.md — the `outage` row names the one case the daemon overrides

See egress-blocked-by-policy-implementation's doc for the full rationale (SC-5840): the daemon's own proxy block record reclassifies the stop into the stage's own *-failed marker, uncharged and said once, with no relaunch until a person edits proxy.domains, restarts the daemon, and Retries the stage — egressBlockedGaveUp holds that refusal even past a restart or the block record's own aging out.

events.name: launch-refused-no-plan
events.where: board_transition.go refuseIfUnplanned — after resumeFixInsteadOfPlanning has declined it
events.guard: the ticket belongs to no fix pipeline (classifyFixPipeline == fixNone); a fix ticket is resumed by fix-resumed-instead-of-planning and no [human:needs-planning] is posted for it at all (SC-5793)
events.doc: The plan executor was launched on a ticket with no plan, so the launch is refused before any agent claims it. The item surfaces back at planning where a human can start one. A relaunch attempted on a card that already failed meets the same gate, so the refusal is also a move a stopped card makes onto itself: the plan is still missing, and the card stays exactly as red as it was. Which of the two determinations a [human:needs-planning] comment is, is its escalation field — plan-stuck for the bound-exhausted escalation, absent for an ordinary refusal (SC-4245); comments posted before the field carry it in their prose and are read by a frozen legacy sentinel. A missing plan is only a refusal for a ticket whose plan a planner writes. A bug or security ticket's plan is written by its own run, so the gate resumes that run instead — this is the marker SC-4244 posted on a bug, asking a person to run planning the pipeline runs itself (SC-5793).

events.name: fix-resumed-instead-of-planning
events.where: board_transition.go launchPlanningOrFix (the isPlanningRetry retry, the forward drop, the decided planning stage) and refuseIfUnplanned → resumeFixInsteadOfPlanning (the plan gate)
events.doc: The machine was about to plan a ticket whose plan its own run writes, and asked first. Every path that starts or restarts planning — the in-place retry the recovery sweep drives, the forward drop, a decision answered while the card sits in planning — and the plan gate that would otherwise refuse an implementation launch for having no plan, all classify the ticket (classifyFixPipeline: the recorded [human:pipeline] marker, then the ticket kind, then the marker heuristic) and resume the fix pipeline rather than dispatching the feature planner. Before this, each site assumed 'in planning, therefore a feature': SC-4244's bug was refused for having no plan, driven into planning, told a person to run planning, and ended with a feature plan (SC-5793). The fix pipeline posts [human:implementation-started] and [human:pipeline], so the card moves to the stage where the work actually is. One case deliberately does not resume: a planner already RUNNING on the ticket withholds, because a second agent on one ticket is worse than one wrong one, and that planner's own ending re-enters this transition.

events.name: plan-redrive-exhausted
events.where: board_transition.go refuseIfUnplanned — the countPlanRefusals >= PlanRedriveBound branch; the marker is composed by planStuckBody
events.doc: The same refusal, taken PlanRedriveBound (3) times, stops driving planning and asks a person instead. It shares the marker of the ordinary refusal so the card renders identically, and carries `escalation: plan-stuck` so the two are told apart by a field rather than by a sentence in the prose (SC-4245). The bound is recounted from the thread, not from daemon state, so it survives a restart and a handover — which is also why the escalation must be recognised on threads written before the field existed. It is said exactly once: the guard that sees a standing escalation as the newest planning-stage marker returns without posting or launching anything.

events.name: stage-relaunch-refused
events.where: internal/daemon/board_transition.go startAgentStage — launchAgent reports launched=false for ErrAgentAlreadyRunning, so no *-started marker is posted; board_retry.go relaunchBounded then rolls the charged attempt back
events.doc: A relaunch the launcher refused because an agent for (key, stage) is already running on this machine. It records NOTHING and the item does not move. That absence is the point: a started marker here would claim a run that never began, re-date StageEnteredAt, and hand the still-running agent another StuckRunningGrace from the very pass meant to reach it — a hung agent was sustained for hours that way (SC-4244). The refusal is still not a failure: no *-failed marker, no error, and the running run's claim and markers stand (SC-2603, SC-1419).

events.name: outage-relaunch-refused
events.where: internal/daemon/board_transition.go startAgentStage via board_retry.go relaunchOutage
events.doc: The uncharged outage re-drive, refused because an agent is already running the stage on this machine. Like stage-relaunch-refused it posts nothing: the standing *-outage marker is left in place for the next tick rather than superseded by a start that did not happen.

events.name: queued-launch-refused
events.where: internal/daemon/board_transition.go startAgentStage via board_options.go pursueDecision and board_reconcile_queued.go reconcileQueuedLaunch
events.doc: The stage a decision named could not be started because an agent on this machine already holds it. The choice stays recorded and the card stays queued — which is now the truthful placement, since no started marker is posted to supersede the choice — and reconcileQueuedLaunch tries again on the next tick past the grace, charging nothing (SC-4244).

events.name: pr-review-launch-refused
events.where: internal/daemon/board_transition.go AdvancePRLoop → launchPRLoopAgent
events.doc: The loop's next step (a fixer) was refused because an agent already owns it. No pr-fix-started marker, so the loop's stage and its round count stay where they are and the running step's Stop event drives the real next action. reconcilePRLoops re-drives the loop every tick behind an alive-guard, so this edge is a live path, not a theoretical one. A launch the doctor's launch gate turns away is a different outcome from this one: it returns ErrLaunchGateRefused rather than the (false, nil) of an owned step, posts no marker and moves no item — a host condition, see not_states / `a host that cannot launch` (SC-5108).

events.name: pr-fix-launch-refused
events.where: internal/daemon/board_transition.go AdvancePRLoop → launchPRLoopAgent
events.doc: The mirror of pr-review-launch-refused: the reviewer relaunch was refused because one already runs. Nothing is recorded, so the loop's clock keeps pointing at the step that is actually going. A launch the doctor's launch gate turns away is a different outcome from this one: it returns ErrLaunchGateRefused rather than the (false, nil) of an owned step, posts no marker and moves no item — a host condition, see not_states / `a host that cannot launch` (SC-5108).

events.name: deploy-fixer-launch-refused
events.where: internal/daemon/board_transition.go deployFailedOrDispatchFixer → dispatchDeployFixer
events.doc: A CI failure routed to the deploy-fixer, refused because a fixer is already running on this machine. No deploy-fix-started marker, so the per-ticket deploy-fix round budget is not spent on a round nobody ran, and the gate is released for the running fixer to re-drive. A launch the doctor's launch gate turns away is different: the deploy DID fail and the fixer was only its remedy, so a gate refusal falls back to deploy-failed naming the CI failure it could not fix, instead of a deploy-fix-started marker nothing re-drives (SC-5108).

events.name: deploy-launch-deferred
events.where: internal/daemon/board_checkout.go awaitCheckoutFree, called first by internal/daemon/board_transition.go openDraftPRAndReview (the board's Deploy drop, the Deploy retry and the outage re-drive all reach it through runDoneStage) and by internal/daemon/deploy_entry.go StartDeploy (the CLI route)
events.doc: The done stage held back because the implementation container for this key was still alive in the checkout it pushes from. It records NOTHING and moves nothing, like the six launch refusals — but unlike them it WAITS first: no reconcile pass drives a plain reviewed card into the done stage (redeploy-after-outage covers only substrate-down), so a refusal here would strand the gesture with nothing to re-drive it. Past DeployCheckoutWaitBound the launch is abandoned, still without a marker, because a container that has outlived its own verdict by fifteen minutes is hung and belongs to the stuck-running sweep — redding the done stage for it would blame the stage that was waiting. The CLI route refuses the same condition back to its caller instead of abandoning silently (ErrDeployCheckoutBusy, the fourth non-failure deploy refusal), since there a person or an agent is waiting for an answer. A liveness answer that cannot be established — a nil lister, a failed listing — is not 'held': stalling every deploy on a docker hiccup costs more than the window it guards.

events.name: reopen-planning
events.where: board_transition.go reopenResolved → launchPlanningOrFix; desktop App.Reopen
events.guard: the ticket belongs to no fix pipeline: classifyFixPipeline returns fixNone from the recorded [human:pipeline] marker, the ticket kind and the marker heuristic, in that order (SC-5793)
events.doc: A person judged the nothing-to-do terminal wrong and re-plans. Separate from every retry gesture because the automatic relaunch drives the identical same-stage request — only an explicitly human call may re-run a clean terminal. A re-open classifies like every other planning start: a [human:nothing-to-do] reached on a bug by a planner that was never its to run re-enters the fix pipeline, not the planner (SC-5793).

events.name: reopen-fix
events.where: board_transition.go reopenResolved — classifyFixPipeline routes to ApplyFix/ApplySecurityFix
events.doc: A person judged the no-fix-needed verdict wrong. The card re-enters its OWN self-planning pipeline, so it re-triages from the top rather than being handed to the plan executor, which would refuse it for having no plan.

events.name: legacy-pr-opened
events.where: board_markers.go orderedMarkerSpecs
events.doc: The PR-opening lifecycle that predates the deploy pipeline. Still classified so threads written before deploy markers existed keep deriving; nothing posts it today.

events.name: legacy-pr-pushed
events.where: board_markers.go orderedMarkerSpecs
events.doc: Legacy: the PR was opened. It classifies as the done stage's DONE state — the same state the merge produces — so on an old thread an opened PR renders where a shipped one does. Recognized for those threads only.

events.name: legacy-pr-failed
events.where: board_markers.go orderedMarkerSpecs
events.doc: Legacy: opening the PR failed. Recognized for pre-deploy-pipeline threads only.

events.name: gate-opens-planning
events.where: internal/daemon/board_transition.go planPrompt — every planning dispatch runs /human-ticket-review as its first phase
events.doc: The ordinary path into the gate, and it moves nothing. The daemon posts planning-started when it dispatches and the gate is the first thing that dispatch runs, so the gate marker arrives AFTER the planning marker — and the card keeps reading as planning, because furthest-stage-wins ranks the planning marker above the gate's backlog-stage one. The gate is a PHASE of planning here, not a stage the item leaves planning for: the same run carries straight on into planning's own work, and planning's markers keep arriving as if the gate had never been a place.
events.prompt: human-ticket-reviewer-agent.md — the gate posts its own ticket-review-started marker

events.name: start-pr-review
events.where: internal/daemon/board_transition.go runDoneStage — the Done stage opens the draft PR and launches the reviewer; isDeployRetry re-enters it on a card whose deploy already failed
events.guard: no board-<key>-implementation or board-<key>-verification container is alive in the checkout — waited for, up to DeployCheckoutWaitBound (deploy-launch-deferred)
events.doc: Dropping on Done. The stage fronts the deploy with the PR review loop rather than posting deploy-started and merging, so the item enters the loop directly and deploying is never recorded on this path. Re-dropping a failed card is the same move, which is why stopped is a source: without it a conflicted deploy would be a dead end escapable only by re-implementing already-reviewed work (SC-735). From stopped the move does one thing more: it mints a [human:deploy-retry] grant worth one automated fix round, so a re-drop on a card whose deploy-fix budget is spent dispatches a fixer instead of re-finding the same conflict and reposting the same failure (SC-5595). Only this edge grants — the machine's own re-entries (redeploy-after-outage, redeploy-when-shippable) and `human deploy` do not, because a machine funding its own budget is not a bound.

events.name: redeploy-after-outage
events.where: internal/daemon/board_transition.go isDeployRetry — an outage card at the Done stage is relaunched in place exactly like a failed one, so the reconcile backoff can re-drive it (SC-2307)
events.guard: no board-<key>-implementation or board-<key>-verification container is alive in the checkout — waited for, up to DeployCheckoutWaitBound (deploy-launch-deferred)
events.doc: The same re-entry as start-pr-review, made by the machine rather than by a person: an infrastructure failure is not the ticket's fault, so nobody should have to drag the card back. Split from start-pr-review because the actor differs, and a state's who_may_act is checked against the transitions that leave it. It is also the way back for a deploy-FIX round or either half of the review→fix loop that hit an outage: the re-drive re-enters the whole done stage, and the round it may re-dispatch is uncharged.

events.name: redeploy-when-shippable
events.guard: the newest done-stage marker is [human:deploy-failed], the forge reports the pull request mergeable with every check passing, no done-stage agent is alive and no deploy is running in this process, the branch resolves here, and the failure is older than FailedRecoveryGrace
events.where: internal/daemon/board_reconcile.go reconcileShippedFailures → redriveShippableDeploy — the re-drive is ReconcileDeps.RetryDeploy, wired to the same in-place done-stage retry transition (isDeployRetry → runDoneStage) the Retry deploy gesture issues
events.doc: The red deploy card, re-observed. The failure was written from one look at the pull request and nothing looked again, so a deploy the machine had already fixed kept asking a person to fix it (SC-3640, on SC-3508's PR #408). Split from start-pr-review because the actor differs — a person dropping on Done versus the machine acting on evidence — and a state's who_may_act is checked against the transitions that leave it. It never fires on an unknown or unreadable state: mergeable-with-everything-green is the only answer it acts on, and a pending check, an absent check list or a probe error all leave the card red. Charges no retry budget: unlike every other recovery from stopped it acts on positive evidence that the deploy is ready to ship, not on a guess that another attempt might work, so a spent budget cannot keep a green, mergeable pull request behind a red card. It mints no deploy-fix grant either: the grant is a person's answer to a spent budget (start-pr-review, SC-5595), and this pass has no person behind it — it reaches the transition through ApplyRetryTransition, whose origin is the machine's, which is what separates it from the gesture since both send an empty Cause.

events.name: gate-verdict-in-planning
events.where: internal/claude/embed/human-ticket-reviewer-agent.md
events.doc: The gate's verdict inside a planning dispatch. It records why, and deliberately does not end the stage — a stop verdict posts planning's own terminal marker alongside it, and ready/reframed simply carry on. Both are why the verdict moves nothing here.

events.name: pr-fix-asks
events.guard: the fixer named two or more directions
events.where: internal/daemon/board_transition.go escalatePRLoop — a fixer that ends needing input becomes a decision rather than a red card
events.doc: The PR fixer hit something only a person can settle. Unlike every other stage-asks, the daemon raises this one rather than the agent: the fixer records its need on exit and the loop turns that into the block, naming the implementation stage so choosing rebuilds through the normal chain and re-adopts the still-open draft PR. The guard is the whole of what makes this a fork: the block carries the fixer's own directions and nothing else. It used to fire on every needs-input exit, filling an empty block with invented answers so it stayed well-formed — which asked a question no one had raised and parked the item on it (SC-3630). A needs-input naming one direction fires pr-fix-takes-sole-direction instead, and one naming none fires pr-loop-escalates.

events.name: pr-fix-takes-sole-direction
events.guard: the fixer named exactly one direction, and the review-round count (the same counter the review→fix loop's outer bound reads) is still under MaxSoleDirectionPursuits (3)
events.where: internal/daemon/board_transition.go escalatePRLoop → pursueSoleDirection, which shares board_options.go pursueDecision with the human path
events.doc: The fixer named one way forward, so there is nothing to decide and the daemon pursues it. A choice between one thing is not a choice — it is a continue button dressed as a fork, and awaiting-decision is the one state the machine may not resolve for itself, so the item must never enter it on a single answer (SC-3630). The choice is recorded with the same marker a human's click records, which is why this lands in queued exactly like decision-made: the record is the audit trail and the consumption signal both, and the item is queued for the implementation stage before it is running in one. Bounded by MaxSoleDirectionPursuits (3) of its own — a FULL implementation-stage rebuild per pursuit is a heavier loop than review→fix, so it keeps its own, smaller cap rather than following DefaultPRReviewRounds (8) up when that one widened for repetition instead of count (SC-5174); past it the direction is reported through pr-loop-escalates rather than taken, so this can never drive an unbounded rebuild loop.

ownership.doc: Who may fire a transition, on two axes. Whose TICKET it is: the assignee, or the reporter when unassigned (daemon.OwnerOf), compared against the machine's declared identity (the .humanconfig `me:` section). Which MACHINE holds a running stage: the daemon that posted the stage's deciding marker (BoardCard.StageDaemonID, from the marker's machine: field). The ticket axis decides whether this machine touches the item at all; the machine axis decides who may take over a stage already running.
rules: The hook path acts only on runs THIS daemon launched. A stage exit arrives as a hook event whose agent name is filled from an environment variable inside the container and forwarded over a route every agent container can reach, and the ticket key used to be parsed straight out of that name — so anything able to send one event could red a ticket and relaunch its stage (SC-4082). The daemon now mints a run id at launch, injects it into the container, and takes the ticket and stage from its own launch record when the event comes back; an id it did not mint moves nothing. Claiming the record also consumes it, so the first exit of a run acts and later events for the same run do not — one run can raise both a StopFailure and a Stop. A run carrying no id predates the registry and falls back to the name, a window one daemon restart wide. A Stop event is not proof the run ended: claude fires one at the end of every main-agent turn, and a board run has one per subagent it waits for, all under the parent's name and run id. So before the record is consumed the watcher asks the container whether claude is still running (the same AgentProcessAlive probe the cleanup listener uses, SC-3785), and an event that outlives its run past cleanupExitWait is left unclaimed — the run's real ending arrives later with the same id (SC-5088).

A machine does autonomous work only on tickets its own person owns: WorkGate.mineToWork in internal/daemon/board_reconcile_gate.go, checked before any intent, so every reconcile pass that writes to a ticket inherits it. Two absences both mean carry on rather than refuse — no identity declared (an install that never said whose work this machine does keeps working as before) and no owner resolvable on the card (an empty owner is unknown, not someone else's, and a tracker that fails to resolve a member name returns exactly that). Only a resolved owner who is demonstrably not this machine's person refuses.

The machine acting on its own initiative — the reconcile takeover pass — refuses a stage another daemon stamped: WorkGate.ownedHereOrUnowned in internal/daemon/board_reconcile_gate.go. An unstamped stage (single-daemon, or a thread written before stamping) is takeable by anyone.
A human gesture is NOT restricted by ownership. Racing a live foreign run is prevented instead by idempotency: a running card refuses every drop (isDuplicateDrop), whichever machine started it.

Ownership is carried to the board as stageDaemonId so a reader can tell a stage owned elsewhere from an unowned one. It is the missing input for liveness across machines: no agent running HERE means dead only if this machine owns the stage.

A stage is CLAIMED before it is launched, and the claim arbitrates between machines only. Every provisioned daemon posts [human:claim] naming the stage, re-reads the thread and launches only if it holds the lowest live claim (internal/daemon/board_claim.go winClaim/claimWon, SC-660 rule 2); a claim stays live until the stage's *-started marker lands at or after it, or until ClaimTTL. A daemon never contends with ITSELF: its own earlier claims for the stage are skipped, because the claim it just posted is the only one it will ever launch. Without that rule two launches that failed after claiming — a *-failed marker does not fulfil a claim — made the next attempt lose the race to its own leftovers, and the stage was unusable for ClaimTTL with nothing on the card to say so (SC-5094). A claim a failed launch left standing still blocks a PEER for the rest of the TTL; it expires rather than being retracted. Losing is silent for a machine-driven move and reported for a person's (see not_states: a stage another daemon claimed).

progress.doc: How an item shows that it is moving. Each in-container phase writes stage.<name> to `human state` with a timestamp — preflight, triage, challenge, fix, verify, review, pr-review, pr-fix, deploy-fix — and the board reads the newest one onto a running OR ended card as `activity`, bounded to the phase records the card's own current run wrote (see note). A card in the done stage's review→fix loop also carries which round it is in (prReviewRound, from chargedPRReviewRounds — the same counter the loop's own outer bound reads, which gives back a round an outage interrupted) against DefaultPRReviewRounds: the two halves alternate their word every round, so a loop going in circles read exactly like one converging.
progress.why: Between implementation-started and ready-for-review an item passes through six phases that all render as one unchanging word. That word is identical at thirty seconds, at fourteen hours, and when the agent behind it is dead, so nothing on the card distinguishes progress from a hang. The phase changing is the signal; its not changing is the other one.
progress.where: internal/board/activity.go; attached in cmd/cmddaemon/daemon.go attachActivity; the round in internal/daemon/board_state.go prLoopRoundFor, copied in internal/board/compose.go
progress.note: Read for a card whose run is working (running) or has ENDED (failed, resolved) — an ended card's phase is how far it got, rendered past-tense with no spinner and no age; a paused (outage) card is excluded because it has not ended. Never invented: a run that recorded no phase shows the stage word exactly as before, and a round that cannot be read is shown as nothing rather than as zero (SC-3656). The stage.* records are keyed on the ticket alone and accumulate for its whole life with no clearing path, so the read is bounded to entries at or after the card's own current run started (BoardCard.StageRunStartedAt) — a stage reaped or crashed before writing anything of its own then shows nothing rather than borrowing an earlier, unrelated stage's leftover phase (SC-3656 PR review finding).

invariants.doc: What each state guarantees while an item sits in it. The transition table says how an item MOVES; these four fields say what is true when it does not, which is the question the pipeline's stuck-card bugs kept turning out to be.

fields.holds: What must be true of the item while it is in this state.
fields.who_may_act: Which declared actors can move it out. An empty list is a true terminal.
fields.stale_when: What makes the state suspect rather than merely slow.
fields.if_nothing_happens: What the machine does on its own when nobody acts — the answer a planner needs and the one a transition table cannot hold.

constants.BoardReconcileInterval: 2m, jittered ±50% — how often the durable pass re-scans open cards (internal/daemon/board_reconcile.go)
constants.StuckRunningGrace: 15m — how long a running card is left alone before liveness is judged
constants.IdleGrace: 3m — how long an agent with NO outstanding work may stay silent before the reap (internal/daemon/agentprogress.go)
constants.WorkingIdleGrace: 30m — how long an agent with outstanding work may stay silent: inside a tool call, waiting on a dispatched subagent, a model request open, OR the model-request state unknown. A dispatch counts because a subagent's events arrive under its parent's name and used to be read as the parent finishing its own work (SC-4900). Unknown takes the generous bound on purpose — the machine must not kill live work because it lost its own bookkeeping (SC-3853).
constants.QueuedLaunchGrace: 2m — how long a card whose decision was answered may sit unstarted before the machine starts it (internal/daemon/board_reconcile_queued.go). Short because the launch is the same call that recorded the choice; it exists only so a tick landing inside that call does not race it.
constants.DefaultStageRetries: 2 — automatic in-place relaunches of one stage (internal/daemon/board_retry.go)
constants.DefaultPRReviewRounds: 8 — the OUTER cap on review→fix rounds (internal/daemon/pr_review_loop.go); the policy bound is repetition — the same blocking finding twice escalates at any round (SC-5174), and since SC-5278 that repeat also fires on the same class of finding recurring in the same file under a fresh slug
constants.DefaultDeployFixRounds: 2 — deploy-fixer dispatches before escalating (internal/daemon/board_transition.go). Per ticket, not per ticket's life: each Retry deploy a PERSON makes on the card mints one further round ([human:deploy-retry], counted by deployFixGrants, spent by the deploy-fix-started marker carrying grant: retry). The machine's own re-drives mint none, so the bound still bounds the machine (SC-5595).
constants.OutageWaitBound: 6h — how long an outage may be relaunched before it is handed to a person (internal/daemon/board_outage.go)
constants.FeedbackTimeout: 30s — how long a stage launch waits for its briefing, the advice block distilled from the project's recorded review findings by one tool-less host model call (internal/daemon/feedback.go). Past it the stage launches without the block: the briefing advises and gates nothing, so it may never delay a launch. A nil Feedback dependency, an empty record or a failed call all produce the same thing — no block — and a prompt byte-identical to one built before the briefing existed (SC-5959).
constants.EgressBlockWindow: 15m — how recent a proxy policy refusal must be to explain a stage that reported an outage (internal/daemon/board_egressblock.go)
constants.MaxSilenceReaps: 3 — silence reaps of one stage before the machine stops relaunching and asks for a person (internal/daemon/board_failure.go). Uncharged against DefaultStageRetries, which is why it needs its own bound. Each reap's *-failed marker records the silence it was judged on as fields (idle, budget, outstanding), and the give-up marker past the bound is a blocker record (kind, evidence quoting every stop, attempted, release) rather than an ordinary stage failure, so a person can tell a hang from a liveness input the daemon could not read without the daemon log (SC-5329).
constants.PlanRedriveBound: 3 — refusals of one unplanned implementation launch before the machine stops driving planning and escalates to a person (internal/daemon/board_transition.go). Counted from the ticket thread rather than daemon state, so it survives a restart; the escalation itself is excluded from the count by its escalation: plan-stuck field.
constants.DeployNoChecksGrace: 3m — how long a pull request head may report NO checks before the gate reads the absence as a repository without CI and proceeds (internal/daemon/board_transition.go deployNoChecksGrace). Below it, absence is pending: the rebased candidate of SC-5083's campaign merged three seconds ahead of its own checks because absence used to read as green (F19).
constants.DeployExternalCheckGrace: 5m — how long a head red ONLY on checks no code change can turn green (a contributor-signature job, a bot comment step) is waited out before the gate stops without dispatching a fixer (internal/daemon/deploy_checks.go deployExternalCheckGrace). Longer than DeployNoChecksGrace because a re-run must register as well as run; far shorter than the 45-minute deploy window because the deploy gate is a process-wide mutex and one card's bot must not starve every other card's deploy (SC-5843).
constants.deploy-card grace (stuckGraceFor, not a: 60m = deployTimeout (45m) + StuckRunningGrace (15m) — how long a card recorded as deploying is left alone before the stuck-running sweep judges it (stuckPastGrace, internal/daemon/board_reconcile.go). The deploy registers no agent for the sweep to probe, so the evidence is the engine's own clock where this machine is running it (its dequeue past deployGate, or the last time the queue moved while it waits), and the marker clock everywhere else.
constants.FailedRecoveryGrace: 5m — how long a failed stage is left to the live exit path before the durable pass may relaunch it (internal/daemon/board_reconcile_failed.go)
constants.FailedRecoveryBound: 6h — how long after its failure a stage may still be relaunched by the durable pass; past it the card is a person's, with the attempts on record
constants.DeployHeadWaitTimeout: 5m — how long the deploy waits for the forge's pull-request resource to report the head the freshness rebase published, before the gate stops instead of reading the replaced tip's verdict (internal/daemon/board_transition.go)
constants.DeployMergeReintegrations: 2 — how often a merge refused for an out-of-date head re-runs the freshness stage and re-gates before the card reds (internal/daemon/board_transition.go)
constants.ClaimTTL: 5m — how long an unfulfilled [human:claim] keeps another MACHINE from claiming the same stage (internal/daemon/board_claim.go). It bounds a claimant that died between claiming and launching; the winner posts *-started within one AddComment, so a live claim is normally fulfilled in seconds. A daemon's own earlier claims never block it at any age (SC-5094).
constants.DeployCheckoutWaitBound: 15m — how long a starting deploy waits for the implementation container to release the bind-mounted checkout before abandoning the launch (internal/daemon/board_checkout.go). Long on purpose: the container's own end frees the tree, and a run merely slow to write its summary must not cost the ticket its deploy.

stage_defaults.doc: The liveness rule for a RUNNING stage, stated once. A state naming one of these in `inherits` takes its stale_when and if_nothing_happens from here, and `note` adds what is true of that state alone. Once rather than per state because it IS one rule: seven copies would need seven coordinated edits to stay true, which is the drift this document exists to prevent — reproduced inside it.

planning.stale_when: Past StuckRunningGrace (15 minutes) with no agent for (key, planning) alive on the machine that owns the stage — or one alive but recording no new phase, which the reconcile pass judges hung and stops before redding. Both halves apply to every stage: reconcileOneStuckCard branches on neither. The grace is skipped when either of two producers shows the stage's agent stopped AFTER the stage was entered while it is absent from the live listing: the execution log's recorded outcome, written before the meta is deleted so it survives the automatic zombie sweep's kill/OOM/crash reap as well as `human agent stop`; or, where the log holds nothing, the agent meta's StoppedAt, written by `human agent list` — the card is then judged on the next tick rather than fifteen minutes later (recordedDeath, SC-5327); the path taken is the same charged vanished-agent one.
planning.if_nothing_happens: The durable reconcile pass (every ~2 minutes) posts [human:planning-failed] and relaunches in place. TWO budgets bound that, and which one is spent depends on how the stage died. A vanished agent is an unexplained death and is charged: DefaultStageRetries (2). An agent this pass judged hung and stopped itself is NOT charged — the work did not fail, a judgement about it did — but repetition is bounded separately by MaxSilenceReaps (3), past which the machine stops relaunching and says a person is needed.

done.stale_when: Past StuckRunningGrace (15 minutes) with NONE of the done stage's agents alive on the machine that owns the stage — or one alive but recording no new phase, which the reconcile pass judges hung and stops before redding. Both halves apply to every stage: reconcileOneStuckCard branches on neither. The done stage is the one stage whose agent name is not derivable from the stage: three agents run under it — board-<key>-prreview (openDraftPRAndReview and each review round), board-<key>-prfix (each fix round) and board-<key>-deployfix (the deploy fixer) — and deploying/ci-gate run no board agent at all. All three are asked (stageAgentNames, internal/daemon/board_stageagents.go), and any one of them alive spares the card; the progress probe is then handed the name that is actually alive. Composing board-<key>-done instead asked about an agent nothing launches, so every deploy fixer that outlived the grace was redded and charged a retry while its container worked (SC-5396). recordedDeath's shortcut (SC-5327) reads the same three names, so a done-stage agent recorded as stopped after the stage was entered is judged on the next tick like any other stage's — EXCEPT while deployEngineActive reports this machine's DeployBranch currently running for the card: the PR loop's merge action and the deploy fixer's post-fix retry both call DeployBranch synchronously with no started marker posted first, so the newest started marker still names the PREVIOUS sub-agent, whose normal, successful exit would otherwise be misread as this window's death and bypass the CI-gate grace above (SC-5396).
done.if_nothing_happens: The durable reconcile pass (every ~2 minutes) posts [human:deploy-failed] and relaunches in place. TWO budgets bound that, and which one is spent depends on how the stage died. A vanished agent is an unexplained death and is charged: DefaultStageRetries (2). An agent this pass judged hung and stopped itself is NOT charged — the work did not fail, a judgement about it did — but repetition is bounded separately by MaxSilenceReaps (3), past which the machine stops relaunching and says a person is needed.

pr-loop.stale_when: NONE of the done stage's three agents alive on the machine that owns the stage — board-<key>-prreview, board-<key>-prfix and board-<key>-deployfix (stageAgentNames / liveStageAgent, internal/daemon/board_stageagents.go), the same ownership qualifier the other stage rules carry. 'No loop HALF alive' is not the rule and was the SC-5591 defect: the deploy fixer posts no loop marker of its own, so a card whose newest marker is still a loop-started marker can be owned by a live fixer — reconcilePRLoops asked only the two halves, re-drove it, and its second merge raced the rebase the fixer was doing and redded the card a minute before the fixer finished. A loop's outcome lives in the owning host's agent state store and is never posted to the tracker, so 'no agent alive HERE' is evidence only on the machine that started it; read as a fleet-wide fact it made a peer red a review that was still running and went on to approve (SC-4025). The generic stuck-running pass deliberately SKIPS a loop card (doneStageLoopActive), so a loop is recovered by re-driving rather than by redding.
pr-loop.if_nothing_happens: reconcilePRLoops re-reads the recorded state and advances or escalates, idempotently. Bounded by repetition — the same blocking finding twice, or the same class of finding recurring in the same file (SC-5278), escalates — and by DefaultPRReviewRounds (8) as the outer cap; past either the loop escalates rather than merging on a state it cannot read (SC-5174). Before acting, a re-drive checks whether the step the fresh thread names has its own agent still alive on the machine that owns the stage (BoardTransitionDeps.LoopStepAlive); if so it stands down and leaves the step to finish rather than escalating over work still in flight (SC-5120). It asks the same question about board-<key>-deployfix, and asks it outside the recorded-outcome short-circuit: the merge that dispatches a deploy fixer runs inside the approved review's own drive, so the newest loop marker still names that review and its recorded approval would otherwise take the re-drive straight back to the merge, against the branch the fixer is rebasing (SC-5591). It runs on the reconcile tick, not on the loop half's exit: reconcilePRLoops is called only from reconcileOnce, so a re-drive lands up to BoardReconcileInterval×(1+BoardReconcileJitter) — one to three minutes — after the reviewer or fixer container ends. The board renders that gap in the machine register rather than as a person's turn: a done/running loop card whose half is recorded as stopped within prLoopRedriveGrace reads AgentRecovering (internal/board/liveness.go), and only past that window does it read AgentDead (SC-5091). A round the done stage's outage marker interrupted is not charged — chargedPRReviewRounds gives it back, the same refund deployFixRounds makes for a fixer round (SC-5627).

not_states.doc: Things that look like places an item can be, and are not. Each was proposed as a state at least once; each fails the same test — you cannot tell an item is there by reading its ticket, because nothing about the ticket changed. Recorded so the argument is made once rather than rediscovered, and so removing one does not read as an oversight.
not_states.an unreadable source: The tracker failed to load, so the board cannot see the item. It WAS a declared state (`unknown`, with `source-unreadable` from 26 states and `source-readable-again` back to `filed`) and it was wrong three ways. The code disagrees: BoardCard.Degraded keeps the card's last-known Stage/State so the board renders it locked in place rather than demoting it (SC-1700) — the item does not move. Its own edges were implemented in internal/board/gate.go and internal/board/compose.go, the only two transitions in this document whose where: was the rendering layer. And its exit landed on `filed`, which said a recovered fetch resets every item to the initial state. The item's own doc string already admitted it: `it says the board could not look, not that the item moved`.
not_states.a closed ticket: Closing takes an item OUT of the pipeline rather than moving it within, so there is no state to name and no edge to add. The one real effect — the ticket's agents are stopped — is a container's story, and docs/reaper.md owns it as `close is cancellation` with its code owner. The board renders it by removing the card (BoardHidden), which is the board's business, not the machine's.
not_states.a host that cannot launch: The daemon refuses to start a stage while a launch-critical doctor check is failing on its host — docker, agent-skills, claude-auth and egress (internal/daemon.LaunchCriticalChecks). Every launch path enforces it, not only the staged one: BoardTransitionDeps.startAgentStage (planning/implementation/verification and the done-stage server route), and the no-claim loop launches BoardTransitionDeps.launchPRLoopAgent (PR review/fix) and BoardTransitionDeps.launchDeployFixAgent (the deploy fixer) — all three route through the shared BoardTransitionDeps.launchGateBlocked. The done-stage server route (internal/daemon/server.go handleBoardTransition) gates too, redundantly with launchPRLoopAgent's own check, because it is the one point that can report the refusal synchronously to the caller rather than losing it in runDoneStage's background goroutine (SC-5108). Nothing is claimed, no marker is posted and the item does not move: the condition belongs to the machine, not to the ticket, and another daemon may serve the same work unimpeded. It is deliberately not `substrate-down` either, which is a stage REPORTING that something it needed was unreachable; here no stage ever started. The two met over SC-4819: a proxy policy that blocked every hostname made every container die at its first model call, and the runs recorded implementation-outage and sat against OutageWaitBound for a local misconfiguration no waiting could clear. The egress check moves that condition here, where the host reports it (doctor / rail LED) and no ticket is blamed for it. claude-auth also fails on evidence the store itself cannot show (SC-5036): a board run that died because the model API refused its login (the exit classified as `model API authentication was refused`, handed to FailureDeps.OnAuthRefused) marks that project's container store refused until the store is rewritten by a fresh /login or a successful refresh, so a rejected refresh token stops the next launch instead of costing it a run. The wipe itself is a THIRD store shape claude-auth's own doctor check judges (SC-5108): Claude Code clears accessToken/refreshToken when the auth server rejects the refresh, leaving subscriptionType/scopes behind, and only both token KEYS present-and-empty together with that surviving evidence reads as signed out — keys simply absent (schema drift) still fails open. Its mid-run sibling is egress-blocked-by-policy-* (one event per stage): the same class of host misconfiguration, met by a stage that had already started, where the run DID report something and the card must therefore say what it was. The launch gate covers only the model API host; any other refused host is only discoverable after a run tried it.
not_states.an idea: An idea-labelled ticket is not inside the machine, even though the machine now acts on it. Membership is the label alone (DeriveBoardCard returns the Ideas stage before reading a single comment), the initial state is `filed`, and promotion is still a label edit that posts no transition marker. What changed with SC-4608 is that a daemon-launched drafter writes the ticket's DESCRIPTION and records provenance in [human:idea-draft] — both listed above as recording content, not movement. A drafting run that dies leaves [human:idea-draft-failed], posted by the daemon rather than the run — the third marker an idea can carry, and the third that moves nothing: it says a draft was attempted and failed, which is a fact about the ATTEMPT, not a position for the ticket. So the drafter acts ON an idea without the idea entering the machine: nothing about where the item is is derived from its markers, there is no stage running, and no marker it carries moves it. A state would have to be something you could read off the ticket, and there is still nothing there to read. SC-4923 widened who may start that drafter — a person may run it from a Product-Backlog card's "Recreate description" — and widened nothing else: the same three markers are now reachable on a ticket that is inside the machine, where they still record content and still move nothing.
not_states.a stage another daemon claimed: A daemon that loses the claim race starts nothing and posts nothing — no marker, no state change, the item does not move — because the daemon that WON is starting it and its markers are the record. It is neither stage-relaunch-refused (one machine declining a second agent for a stage it is already running) nor a failure: nothing reds, and nothing is charged against the retry budget. Two things happen on the losing side, and before SC-5094 neither did: the host logs the race with the winning claim id and daemon, and a launch a PERSON asked for is refused back to the board with the winner named (ErrClaimLost, returned through BoardTransitionDeps.ApplyTransition when the request carries no Cause). A machine-driven move — the build→review chain, an automatic retry, a decision the daemon pursued for itself — stays silent: the winner's own markers move the card within seconds and nobody is waiting on an answer. The residue is the peer case: a claim left standing by a failed launch still blocks another machine until ClaimTTL, since nothing retracts it.
